english_verification.review_scope: Representative current-Mod opening history, mission and event text; fixed-revision English Wiki historical passages read for the hold, Jadefall, protectorate expansion and rebellions. Wiki is historical/lore support only, not current-mechanics proof; no exhaustive mission or national-idea audit. Native English idea names/descriptions were compared by localisation key with the current Mod. Wide line ranges locate separately read passages, not exhaustive coverage. No formal validator, build, browser or gameplay test was run.
unresolved: Existing idea-effect displays include +100% diplomatic reputation and +2500% same-continent liberty desire. These inherited units are retained, not newly validated or silently corrected.

rationale.complexity: Subjects, rune combinations and religious routes overlap.
rationale.dark_story: A controlling protectorate system exists, but systematic personal harm is not established.
rationale.difficulty: The late-game network is cumbersome to manage; no hands-on playtest was performed.
rationale.diplomacy: A special subject network determines the campaign's success.
rationale.early_pressure: The starting core is small, but friendly states and special institutions help.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Runes and Dwarven Pantheon knowledge are important parts of play.
rationale.narrative_density: The rise and fall of the hold, the search for scattered kin and the rebuilding of influence form a continuous story.
rationale.tall_play: The hold and rune systems make compact domestic development central.
rationale.trade_economy: The mountain core and surface partners benefit from mutually useful trade.
rationale.warfare: Warfare relies mainly on protectors and subjects.

identity.appearance: A one-province Nephrite Dwarf hold in 1444, following the Dwarven Pantheon and possessing historic friends nearby.
identity.formation_scope: Y63 unifies Haless through its protector network; no Tag change is required.
predecessors: Grônstunad (setting source, not a playable predecessor Tag).

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: Verkal Ozovar has loomed high over the lands of the Hinphat since they were but mere tribes roaming the plains, shadowed by the Phokhao Range. For eons we have been their guiding hand as their Mountain Kings, uplifting them into civility in return for regular tribute and servitude.
description.text_en: Verkal Ozovar has loomed high over the lands of the Hinphat since they were but mere tribes roaming the plains, shadowed by the Phokhao Range. For eons we have been their guiding hand as their Mountain Kings, uplifting them into civility in return for regular tribute and servitude.

description.text: When the holds of the Jade Mines fell, their inhabitants were forced to flee, trekking through the exotic and diverse realms of Haless before finally reaching our mighty Nephrite Hold. The refugees picked up on as much knowledge as they could during their travels, developing new insights into their previously conservative dwarven mindset. With such extensive knowledge of cultural customs from across Haless, our emissaries have an easy time ingratiating themselves with foreign powers.

description.text: Most that look upon the Phokhao range see only the rough, jagged stone of the mountains, not knowing of the great wealth of gems and ores hidden deep within, only accessible to those with the ingenuity and determination of a dwarf.
description.text_en: Most that look upon the Phokhao range see only the rough, jagged stone of the mountains, not knowing of the great wealth of gems and ores hidden deep within, only accessible to those with the ingenuity and determination of a dwarf.

description.text: Many of our displaced kin, heirs of the Jadefall, reside in small surface towns and squalorous slums across Haless, unable to truly find new homes among the humans and harimari. This is a call for them to flock to the verdant gates of Verkal Ozovar, to finally reside among brothers once again.

description.text: Grônstunad was the greatest hold of the eastern Serpentspine, its power even rivalling that of Amldihr and outlasting the old capital of Aul-Dwarov. Even she was not to last however, as those goblinoid bastards overran her gates and desecrated her hallowed halls of jade. We are the descendents and heirs to those that escaped the fall of Grônstunad, and we are determined to live up to our illustrious legacy.

description.text:
Magic comes easier to the inhabitants of Verkal Ozovar than most other dwarves in the form of runesmithing, though the arcane arts may still be a relative rarity amongst our people compared to the likes of humans or elves.

Enough runesmiths practice their craft within our halls to risk themselves on the frontlines of battle, concocting grand runic batteries to fell our foes in addition to traditional spellcraft.

description.text: The Viridescent Legion is the elite guard of Verkal Ozovar, each member personally chosen by the king of our hold to serve for life and clad in opulent enchanted Nephrite armor. These fine warriors lead the armies of Ozovar as their gleaming vanguard, standing as the pride of the Citadel of the East.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who only want to annex land personally and do not want to manage subject loyalty and diplomacy.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Hold and develop the mountain fortress, gradually gather protectors, and organize Halessi wars through runes and subjects.
player_overview.overview: Verkal Ozovar is an ancient Nephrite Dwarf hold, in 1444 guarding only a small core while its former subjects around it have gradually become independent. Your goal is not to swallow every province like an ordinary empire, but to build a one-province fortress, reconnect the protector network, configure runes and search for scattered kin. Its strength comes from other countries' cooperation and obedience; the real difficulty is maintaining subject loyalty, balancing protection and control, and managing a vast indirect realm.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy compact development, subject networks, rune combinations and indirect rule.
signature_features: Compact one-province development and a special protector-subject network spanning Haless coexist.
The rune interface lets you adjust combinations for construction, war and diplomacy.
The Jade search links an ancient diaspora to later religious and knowledge routes.
player_overview.tagline: Stay in the hold and rebuild influence across Haless through protectors, runes and allies.

reasons: A sharp contrast between a one-province fortress and a huge subject network.
The rune interface creates different combinations for management and war.
Nephrite Dwarf history gives Halessi expansion a motive.
warnings: Late-game performance concerns are supported only by older player reports.

positive_indicators: Providing knowledge and security to surrounding communities.
Protecting the hold and trading with partners.
values.rationale: Knowledge-sharing, protection and trade have positive evidence; old history and current mechanics retain hierarchical control over subjects, so protection cannot be called equal autonomy, while there is not enough evidence to equate it with slavery.
red_flags: The protector relationship contains structural power asymmetry.
The old empire faced repeated human independence rebellions.
